Title: Diagnosis of test `testPartialReadTruncatedData`

Details:
The test `testPartialReadTruncatedData` in `PythonTruncatedBzip2Test` fails with an IOException indicating "unexpected end of stream" while reading from a BZip2 compressed data source. The error stack trace points to the method `BZip2CompressorInputStream.bsR` followed by subsequent calls within the bzip2 decompression process.

This suggests that during decompression in `BZip2CompressorInputStream`, the input stream ended prematurely, likely due to truncated or incomplete compressed data. The read chain (`read()` -> `read0()` -> internal block setup methods) attempts to process and decode blocks within the compressed stream. When the data ends unexpectedly during these steps, the exception is raised.

This method `.bsR(int)` (and indirectly `.bsGetUByte()` and `.initBlock()`, etc.) seems to perform bitstream reading and block initialization, respectively, which would be sensitive to truncated input.

The key point is that the decompressor does not appear to handle truncated data gracefully — it throws an IOException immediately when encountering premature end of stream, instead of possibly signaling EOF or partial read gracefully as the test might expect.

Next step is to review the code inside `BZip2CompressorInputStream.bsR(int)` to understand how end of stream is handled and why the exception is thrown.
